package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious document, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of Windows and Windows Server with MSDT enabled
package_info.why_malicious: The document abuses the ms-msdt:// URL protocol handler to trigger the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) from within a Word document, enabling remote code execution with the privileges of the user. This allows attackers to install programs, steal data, or create new accounts, representing a critical security risk.

execution_context.trigger: document open or preview (import-time in Word)
execution_context.file_location: Word document (remote template reference in document XML)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open or preview, the Word document uses the remote template feature to fetch an external HTML file from an attacker-controlled server, enabling further code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Word documents should not fetch remote HTML templates, especially from untrusted sources. This is a common vector for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents reference local resources or trusted remote templates, not attacker-controlled domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Corporate templates may be hosted on internal servers, but not on random internet domains.
key_indicators: Remote template URL to untrusted domain

execution_context.trigger: HTML file loaded by Word (runtime in mshtml)
execution_context.file_location: payload.html (served by attacker, loaded by Word)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the HTML payload is loaded by Word, JavaScript redirects the browser to a specially crafted ms-msdt:// URI, triggering the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool with attacker-supplied parameters, leading to arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTML loaded in this context should not invoke OS-level protocol handlers, especially diagnostic tools with code execution capabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTML templates do not redirect to ms-msdt:// or similar protocol handlers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Very rare; protocol handlers may be used for deep OS integration, but not from untrusted HTML in Office documents.
key_indicators: Use of ms-msdt:// URI in HTML/JavaScript
Redirection to protocol handler from Office context

execution_context.trigger: MSDT launched via ms-msdt:// protocol (runtime, child process of Word)
execution_context.file_location: Invoked by ms-msdt:// URI (no file, process context)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ms-msdt:/id PCWDiagnostic /skip force /param ... (parameters include PowerShell command to download and execute payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When MSDT is launched via the ms-msdt:// protocol, attacker-supplied parameters cause MSDT to execute arbitrary PowerShell code, which can download and run further malware or steal data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: MSDT should not be invoked with arbitrary parameters from untrusted sources, especially those that execute PowerShell.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Diagnostic tools are not expected to execute arbitrary code from Office documents.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: MSDT may be used for legitimate troubleshooting, but not with attacker-controlled scripts.
key_indicators: ms-msdt:// protocol invocation with PowerShell payload
Execution of code in context of Office process

attack_chain.action: Victim opens or previews a malicious Word document, which references a remote template.
attack_chain.leads_to: Word fetches and loads attacker-controlled HTML.

attack_chain.action: Word loads the remote HTML payload, which redirects to the ms-msdt:// protocol handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: MSDT is launched with attacker-supplied parameters.

attack_chain.action: MSDT executes attacker-supplied PowerShell code, leading to arbitrary code execution (malware installation, data theft, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: system compromise, data exfiltration, or further malware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Office document fetching remote HTML templates
ms-msdt:// protocol handler invoked from Office context
PowerShell execution as a child of msdt.exe or WINWORD.EXE
file_indicators: Word documents with INCLUDEPICTURE or remote template fields
network_indicators: Office applications making HTTP/HTTPS requests to untrusted domains
Connections to attacker infrastructure (e.g., tibet-gov.web.app, coolrat.xyz)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Office processes for child processes invoking msdt.exe, especially with suspicious command-line parameters. Detect Office documents that reference remote templates or INCLUDEPICTURE fields pointing to external domains. Inspect network traffic for Office applications making unexpected external requests. Look for ms-msdt:// protocol handler invocations in logs, and PowerShell execution chains originating from Office or msdt.exe.
